The shrine was historically Ranked as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}. It was formed during the Meiji period through the merger of '''Takeda Shrine''', a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and '''Suga Shrine'''. 

The shrine enshrines {{ill|Take Nunokawa Wake no Mikoto|ja|武渟川別|zh|武渟川别|qid=Q11546050|lt=Takenuokawa Wake no Mikoto}} (the former deity of Takeda Shrine) and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} (the former deity of Suga Shrine).

It is a provincial soja with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

== History ==
'''Takeda Shrine''' has an but it is said to have been founded by the {{ill|Yūki no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|結城国造}} lineage of the {{ill|Takeda no Omi|ja|竹田臣}}, who enshrined their ancestor, Takenuokawa Wake no Mikoto. This deity was one of the {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|ja|四道将軍}}, a group of four generals dispatched to pacify and develop the eastern provinces. The shrine is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} under "Takeda Shrine of Yūki District, Shimōsa Province," making it one of the 11 shrines listed for Shimōsa Province. In 1764 (Hōreki 14), the shrine was relocated to the grounds of {{ill|Jōkoku-ji|ja|乗国寺}}, a {{ill|Sōtō|en|Sōtō|qid=Q749085|lt=Sōtō Zen}} temple that serves as the ancestral temple of the {{ill|Yūki clan|en|Yūki clan|qid=Q2975399|lt=Yūki clan}}.

'''Suga Shrine''' was established in 1242 (Ninji 3) when the ruling {{ill|Yūki clan|en|Yūki clan|qid=Q2975399|lt=Yūki clan}} invited the deity from {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}} in {{ill|Owari Province|ar|أواري|ca|Província d'Owari|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆوواری|cs|Provincie Owari|de|Provinz Owari|es|Provincia de Owari|eu|Owari probintzia|fa|ولایت اوواری|fi|Owarin provinssi|fr|Province d'Owari|gl|Provincia de Owari|hak|Owari-koet|id|Provinsi Owari|it|Owari (provincia)|ja|尾張国|ko|오와리국|lt|Ovario žemė|nl|Owari (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Owari|pt|Província de Owari|ru|Овари (провинция)|simple|Owari Province|sk|Owari (provincia)|sr|Провинција Овари|tr|Owari (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Оварі|vi|Tỉnh Owari|wuu|尾张国|zh|尾張國|zh_min_nan|Owari-kok|zh_yue|尾張國|qid=Q514506|lt=Owari Province}}, naming it '''Tenno-sha''' (天王社). In 1343 (Kōei 2), {{ill|Yūki Naotomo|ja|結城直朝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yūki Naoasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11606616}} designated it as one of the '''Yūki Seven Shrines''' (結城七社) and made it the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|qid=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (main provincial shrine) of {{ill|Yūki District|ja|結城郷}}. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu Bunri}} reforms in 1868 (Meiji 1), the shrine was renamed '''Suga Shrine'''. 

In 1870 (Meiji 3), Takeda Shrine was separated from Jōkoku-ji and merged with Suga Shrine, forming '''Takeda Suga Shrine'''. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}}, and in 1930 (Shōwa 5), it was elevated to a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度}}.

'''Takeda Suga Shrine''' (健田須賀神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Yūki, Ibaraki|ar|يوكي (إيباراكي)|arz|يوكى (بلده فى ايباراكى)|azb|یوکی، ایباراکی|ce|Юки (гӀала)|ceb|Yūki-shi|de|Yūki|eo|Juki|es|Yūki (Ibaraki)|fa|یوکی، ایباراکی|fi|Yūki|fr|Yūki (Ibaraki)|gl|Yūki|id|Yūki, Ibaraki|it|Yūki (Ibaraki)|ja|結城市|ko|유키시|mg|Yūki|mzn|یوکی، ایباراکی|nl|Yuki|pl|Yūki (Ibaraki)|pt|Yuki (Ibaraki)|ro|Yūki|ru|Юки (город)|sv|Yūki, Ibaraki|tg|Юки|th|ยูกิ (จังหวัดอิบารากิ)|tl|Yuki, Ibaraki|tr|Yūki|tt|Юки (шәһәр)|uk|Юкі (Ібаракі)|ur|یکی، اباراکی|uz|Yuki (Ibaraki)|vi|Yūki, Ibaraki|war|Yūki, Ibaraki|zh|結城市|zh_classical|結城市|zh_min_nan|Yuki-chhī|zh_yue|結城|qid=Q847569|lt=Yūki, Ibaraki}}, Japan. The shrine is classified as a former Prefectural Shrine and was formed in the Meiji period by merging the {{ill|Takeda Shrine|ja|健田神社}} and {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, with the former being a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

The shrine enshrines {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武渟川別命}}, the deity of the original Takeda Shrine, and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}, the deity of the original Suga Shrine.

== History ==
The '''Takeda Shrine''' has an unclear founding date but is said to have been established by the Yūki Province {{ill|Yūki clan|ja|結城国造}}, who enshrined their ancestral deity {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武渟川別命}}. Takenouchi no Sukune was one of the {{ill|Shido Shōgun|ja|四道将軍}}, credited with pacifying and developing eastern Japan. The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} as "Kenda Shrine" under the 11 shrines of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|qid=Q1053695|lt=Shimousa Province}}. In 1764 (Hōreki 14), the shrine was relocated to the grounds of {{ill|Jōkoku-ji|ja|乗国寺}}, a {{ill|Sōtō|en|Sōtō|qid=Q749085|lt=Sōtō Zen}} temple.

The '''Suga Shrine''' was established in 1242 (Ninji 3) by the {{ill|Yūki clan|en|Yūki clan|qid=Q2975399|lt=Yūki clan}}, who brought its deity from the {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}} in Owari Province. Initially called "Tennōsha," it became the collective shrine for Yūki district in 1343 (Kōei 2) under the Yūki clan. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu bunri|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535}} of the Meiji period, the name was changed from Tennōsha to Suga Shrine.

In 1870 (Meiji 3), the Takeda Shrine separated from Jōkoku-ji and was merged with the Suga Shrine to form the '''Takeda Suga Shrine'''. It was Ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and elevated to a Prefectural Shrine in 1930 (Shōwa 5).
